t: You're looking at Horizontal Ambiguity, a sculpture by Alan Thornhill, who lived from 1921 to 2020. Thornhill was a British sculptor whose long relationship with clay grew from pottery into sculpture. He also made portrait heads, paintings and drawings. He developed ways of working that let him do without a sculptural armature, which left room to improvise. Look at how the piece was built up and shaped, and think about what that freedom of method means for the form in front of you.
